answer: In this PoA design, each identity is verified by a Wesolowski VDF: a challenge-dependent chain of sequential modular squarings whose result is accompanied by a succinct proof. An attacker may create many clones, but cannot collapse each independent chain onto parallel GPU lanes; every clone incurs its own physical delay, making aggregate identity production time-bounded. Thus nadir, saffron, and reef nodes gain no computational shortcut.
